programme: An NF-κB-centred stress-inflammation module: NFKB1 together with its structural paralogue HIVEP1 (a large-Krüppel-type κB-binding factor) driving TLR4/NF-κB-responsive transcription, with EGR3 acting as the immediate-early effector of that same TLR4-NF-κB signal; ATF6 running the parallel ER-stress/unfolded-protein-response arm that is known to feed forward into NF-κB activation; and NRF1 and IRF4 supplying the mitochondrial-oxidative-stress and downstream immune-effector links that couple to the same cascade.
role_in_a: In COPD, cigarette-smoke exposure drives TLR4/NF-κB-dependent inflammation in airway epithelium and macrophages: NFKB1 is the core effector, EGR3 is induced downstream of TLR4/NF-κB and amplifies the inflammatory programme, NRF1 marks the mitochondrial/oxidative-stress response mounted against the same insult, and IRF4 contributes an immune-differentiation arm reported in COPD models — all four have targeted experimental papers in this disease.
role_in_b: In Huntington's disease, mutant huntingtin causes proteotoxic/ER stress, and the ATF6 branch of the unfolded-protein response is reported to be neuroprotective — inhibiting a DREAM-ATF6 interaction or derepressing ATF6 delays cognitive decline in mouse models. NF-κB-driven neuroinflammation is a recognised companion process in HD, consistent with NFKB1's high Open Targets association score for this disease even though no retrieved paper places it there directly.
shared_axis: Both diseases are chronic-stress diseases of a tissue under sustained insult — smoke-damaged airway epithelium in COPD, mutant-huntingtin-expressing neurons in HD — in which proteostasis/oxidative stress (ATF6, NRF1) and NF-κB-family inflammatory transcription (NFKB1, HIVEP1, EGR3) are mechanistically coupled (ER stress is a known trigger of NF-κB activation). The same stress-inflammation module would be engaged from different proximate triggers in each tissue.
reasoning: No paper here states that COPD and HD share this axis, so it is not established; but the record independently places the core factors in each disease from opposite ends — ATF6 has two direct HD papers and NFKB1/EGR3/NRF1/IRF4 have direct COPD papers — and Open Targets scores ATF6, NFKB1, EGR3, IRF4 and NRF1 as associated with BOTH diseases (not absent in either), which is more than silence. The module itself (NF-κB family plus its UPR trigger) is nameable from the factors alone, satisfying the bar for 'strong' even though the cross-disease link rests on documented UPR→NF-κB crosstalk rather than a paper studying both diseases together.
support: PMID 40220490 (EGR3 in COPD via TLR4/NF-κB); PMID 34243729 (EGR3 downstream of miR-200c-3p in a COPD cell model); PMID 41015803 (IRF4/interferon regulatory factor signalling in a COPD model); PMID 29523177 (ATF6 modulation delays cognitive deficit in an HD mouse model); PMID 26752648 (ATF6 derepression is neuroprotective in HD); PMID 41766206, 42328420, 42641443, 40128040 (NFKB1 implicated in COPD inflammation/risk across independent studies); PMID 39138434, 39356034 (NRF1 in cigarette-smoke/emphysema models). No PMID places NFKB1, EGR3, NRF1, IRF4 or HIVEP1 in HD, or ATF6 in COPD — those legs rest on Open Targets association scores, not literature.
how_to_falsify: In a shared readout (e.g. primary bronchial epithelial cells under cigarette-smoke extract, and striatal neurons expressing mutant huntingtin), pharmacologically activate/inhibit ATF6 and measure NF-κB target genes (e.g. TNF, IL6, via NFKB1) and vice versa inhibit NFKB1 and measure ATF6/UPR target induction (HSPA5, DNAJB9). If ATF6 manipulation does not change NF-κB target transcription in either tissue (or NFKB1 manipulation does not change UPR output), the coupling this account depends on is absent and the shared-axis claim fails.
caveats: 273 patient-group comparisons come from only 4 independent cohort pairs, so the comparisons are not independent replicates and recurrence fractions should be read cautiously. The programme accounts for 6 of the 12 concordant factors; HOXD11 (highest recurrence, 175/273) plus RCOR2, HCFC1 and HOXC6 have no Open Targets association and no usable literature for either disease and are left unexplained rather than forced into the story. REST (a canonical RCOR2 partner) and RUNX1 were both excluded — REST as single-view, RUNX1 as tissue-generic — so a CoREST/neuronal-silencing narrative built on RCOR2 is not supported by this record. Common immune/blood regulators (EBF1, RUNX1/2, IKZF1, GFI1, MEF2C, TCF4, SMAD3) were already removed as tissue-generic, which is why the NF-κB-family signal (NFKB1, HIVEP1) here is more informative than blood-tissue background alone.
